place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 外门 · 大通铺
place.en: Chending Temple · The outer court · the long dormitory bed

_weather: 「就着窗外的月光，给家里写第一封信」: a moonlit night (Hanli 2026-10-14: 「可以，月夜标成晴」)

setup.zh: 腊月初八的黄昏。观主把玉盒子放在祁长松手里；你是伙房大娘拿晾衣杆从树上捅下来的。夜里，周衡结「另议」那一笔；阿禾押的那一文，输了。
setup.en: Dusk on the eighth of the twelfth month. The abbot sets the jade box in Qi Changsong's hands; you are poked down out of the tree by the kitchen auntie with a clothes pole. At night Zhou Heng settles the 'to be settled'; the one cash Ahe bet is lost.

recap.zh: 筑基丹归了祁长松；观主说：「四层了。过了年，搬到内门去。」褚先生搭了你的右腕：「马家那个，不是反噬。」大比那夜，周衡结了巡夜那一笔，十块灵石；阿禾押的一文输了。柴房里，两根熬白了的牛骨头喂进饭桶，铁锅里滚起了火锅，银月吃上了火锅。孙二狗托你写信：「娘，我倒了七回，起来了七回。」你给家里写了第一封信：「娘，漏勺也能打水。」夜里银月说，镜子裂的那一下，那头有人：「叫徐州那个，十月去邺城等着。」
recap.en: The Foundation pill went to Qi Changsong; the Abbot said: "Fourth layer now. After the New Year, move to the inner sect." Master Chu took your right wrist: "That Ma boy — it wasn't backlash." The night of the contest Zhou Heng settled the night-watch account — ten spirit stones; the one cash Ahe bet was lost. In the woodshed two soup bones boiled white went into the Rice Bucket, a hotpot came bubbling up in the iron pot, and Yinyue had her hotpot at last. Sun Ergou asked you to write his letter: "Ma, I went down seven times and got up seven times." You wrote your first letter home: "Ma, a leaky ladle can carry water too." That night Yinyue said someone was at the other end when the mirror cracked: "Tell the one from Xu Province to go to Ye in the tenth month and wait."

zh: 「叫徐州那个，十月去邺城等着。」
en: "Fourth layer now. After the New Year, move to the inner sect."
"Shopkeeper, the one cash I bet — lost."
"Tell the one from Xu Province to go to Ye in the tenth month and wait."

story.zh:
冠军，筑基丹一枚。观主把那只玉盒子放在祁长松手里。祁长松双手接了，跪下，磕了一个头，起来的时候，眼眶是红的。

小满是伙房大娘拿晾衣杆从树上捅下来的。观主从竹椅上站起来，走到他跟前，温和地道：「四层了。过了年，搬到内门去。」顿了一顿，又道：「沉鼎秘境里，有一间石室。三百年，没人进去过……」他没说完，拍了拍他的肩膀，转身走了。

马小宝是给两个跟班架回大通铺的，两只眼睛拿布蒙着，手里还攥着那面裂了的镜子。褚先生翻开他的眼皮看了一眼：「灼着了。蒙三天，瞎不了。」瞿老站在台阶上，拄着扫帚，也在看。可瞿老看的不是他，是祁长松手里那只玉盒子。

台阶底下，褚先生在等他：「把腕子伸过来。」小满把左腕递过去。褚先生不接，道：「不是这一只，另一只。」小满站了一会儿，把右手从袖子里伸了出来。松了手，道：「脉上是四层，跟名册上一样。」走出去三步，头也不回，又补了一句：「马家那个，不是反噬。」

天黑下来的时候，周衡在执事房里点上了那半根蜡烛。「另议的那一笔，今天议——」他从抽屉里一块一块地往外数，「——一、二、三……十块。」周衡道：「腊八结账，结在晚上。」小满走到门口，回过头来叫了一声：「……周师兄。」周衡道：「嗯，还有事？」小满说：「有前途。」周衡咳嗽一声，耳朵根「腾」地红了。

阿禾把那张折成一小块的纸条打开，摊在秤盘上，面无表情：「掌柜的，我押的那一文，输了。」钱掌柜道：「输了。」阿禾站了一站，从怀里摸出小本子，翻开，拿炭条一笔一笔地写，写完了，合上，转身走了。

他站在老槐树底下，先是笑，笑着笑着，眼睛便热了。那一文钱，是她娘缝在她衣角里的。阿禾走出去几步，回过头来，看了他一眼，道：「你今天没藏。」小满没说话，右手攥着，没有张开。她只说了两个字：「藏好。」

那天夜里，柴墩上支起了一口豁了边的铁锅。银月钻了出来，蹲在锅沿上，两只前爪举过头顶：「今晚火锅——耶～～」孙二狗揉了揉眼睛，看看锅，看看小满，小声道：「沈师兄，这锅……漏？」小满道：「是有点漏。」

这一夜，满观说的都是一件事：「他凭什么？」「运气。」「运气能连着撞上四回？」大通铺上，马小宝裹着被子抖了半夜，只说了一句：「镜子照着他……他手底下，亮了。」没人理他。

孙二狗摸到他铺前，小声道：「卢师兄那一脚，你替我还了。」小满道：「他自己踩滑的。」「我坐在石阶上，闻见花椒味了。」「沈师兄，明天替我写封信。就写：娘，我倒了七回，起来了七回。」他顿了一顿：「别写是谁把我打倒的。」
story.en:
The champion: one Foundation Pill. The Abbot put the jade case into Qi Changsong's hands. Qi Changsong took it in both hands, knelt, and knocked his head to the ground once; when he got up, the rims of his eyes were red.

Xiaoman was poked down out of the tree by the kitchen woman with a washing pole. The Abbot rose from the bamboo chair, came up to him, and said mildly: "Fourth layer now. After New Year, move to the inner sect." He paused, and said: "In the Sunken Cauldron secret realm there's a stone chamber. For three hundred years, nobody has been in it..." He didn't finish. He patted Xiaoman's shoulder, turned and left.

Ma Xiaobao was carried back to the long bunk between two hangers-on, both eyes bound with cloth, the cracked mirror still gripped in his hand. Master Chu lifted his eyelid and looked: "Scorched. Keep them bound three days, and he won't go blind." Elder Qu stood on the steps, leaning on his broom, watching too. But what Elder Qu was watching wasn't him. It was the jade case in Qi Changsong's hands.

At the foot of the steps, Master Chu was waiting for him: "Give me your wrist." Xiaoman held out his left wrist. Master Chu didn't take it: "Not that one. The other." Xiaoman stood a moment, then brought his right hand out of his sleeve. He let go and said: "The pulse says fourth layer, same as the register." Three steps off, without looking back, he added one thing: "The Ma boy. That wasn't backlash."

When it got dark, Zhou Heng lit the half candle in the stewards' office. "The item to be settled separately, settled today—" He counted them out of the drawer one at a time. "—one, two, three... ten." Zhou Heng said: "Accounts close at Laba. They close in the evening." Xiaoman went to the door, turned round and said: "...Senior Brother Zhou." Zhou Heng said: "Mm. Something else?" Xiaoman said: "You'll go far." Zhou Heng coughed, and the roots of his ears went red all at once.

Ahe unfolded the little square of paper and laid it flat on the steelyard pan, her face blank: "Shopkeeper, that copper I bet. It lost." Shopkeeper Qian said: "It lost." Ahe stood a moment, took her little notebook out of her robe, opened it, and wrote in it stroke by stroke with charcoal; when she had finished she closed it, turned and left.

Xiaoman stood under the old pagoda tree and first laughed; and laughing, his eyes went hot. That one copper coin her mother had sewn into the hem of her clothes. Ahe went a few steps, looked back, gave him one look, and said: "You didn't hide today." Xiaoman said nothing. His right hand was clenched, and he didn't open it. She said only two words: "Hide well."

That night, on the chopping block stood an iron pot with a chipped rim. Yinyue came out, crouched on the pot's rim, and raised both front paws over her head: "Hotpot tonight—yaaay~~" Sun Ergou rubbed his eyes, looked at the pot, looked at Xiaoman, and said quietly: "Senior Brother Shen, this pot... does it leak?" Xiaoman said: "It leaks a bit."

That night the whole abbey talked about one thing. "How did he do it?" "Luck." "Luck four times running?" In the long bunk, Ma Xiaobao lay wrapped in his quilt shaking half the night, and said only one thing: "The mirror shone on him... and under his hand, something lit up." Nobody paid him any attention.

Sun Ergou felt his way to Xiaoman's bunk and said quietly: "That stamp of Senior Brother Lu's. You paid it back for me." Xiaoman said: "He slipped by himself." "I was sitting on the steps. I smelled the Sichuan pepper." "Senior Brother Shen, write a letter for me tomorrow. Just write: Ma, I fell down seven times and got up seven times." He paused. "Don't write who knocked me down."

story_full.zh:
冠军，筑基丹一枚。观主把那只玉盒子放在祁长松手里，玉盒子玉色青白，盒盖上贴着一道封条，封条上盖着观主的大印；盒子还没打开，一缕清苦的药香已经从缝里渗出来，冷冷的，像腊月清早的松针，前排的人不由自主地吸了一口气，吸完了，胸口里一凉，又一热。祁长松双手接了，跪下，磕了一个头，起来的时候，眼眶是红的。周衡把那本蓝布面的名录摊开，往前翻了几十页，翻到划了一道的那一页，看了一眼，才又翻回来，翻到新的一页，把笔递给了唱名的执事。

小满是伙房大娘拿晾衣杆从树上捅下来的。大娘一面捅，一面念叨：「……你这孩子。」

他落了地，往台下走，人堆自己往两边分开一条道。他走过的地方，没有人笑他，好些人看他，看得很久。观主从竹椅上站起来，走到他跟前，温和地道：「四层了。过了年，搬到内门去。」顿了一顿，又道：「沉鼎秘境里，有一间石室。三百年，没人进去过……」他没说完，拍了拍他的肩膀，转身走了。小满站在那里，后背上的汗，一下子全冒了出来。

马小宝是给两个跟班架回大通铺的，脸上糊着伙房大娘的獾油，两只眼睛拿布蒙着，手里还攥着那面裂了的镜子，倒下去的时候也没撒手。褚先生翻开他的眼皮看了一眼：「灼着了。蒙三天，瞎不了。」他五层了，内门的名册上也添了他，当晚便有一位姓崔的长老差人来，把他收进了门下；可他一路上一句话也没说，只把蒙着布的脸扭过去，朝着泗水那边。马家的船已经开走了。

小满往山门那边望了一眼。瞿老站在台阶上，拄着扫帚，也在看。可瞿老看的不是他，是祁长松手里那只玉盒子。那一眼很长，长得不像是在看一只盒子，倒像是在看一件很多年以前的旧事。然后瞿老转过身去，扫地了。

台阶底下，褚先生在等他。人都往伙房那边散了，老先生一个人站在那里，冲他伸出两根指头：「把腕子伸过来。」小满把左腕递过去。褚先生不接，道：「不是这一只，另一只。」小满站了一会儿，把右手从袖子里伸了出来。褚先生搭了很久，久到山门那边瞿老的扫帚又响了起来。松了手，道：「脉上是四层，跟名册上一样。」捋了一下山羊胡子，转身走了，走出去三步，头也不回，又补了一句：「马家那个，不是反噬。」

天黑下来的时候，周衡在执事房里点上了那半根蜡烛。小满进去的时候，他已经翻开了巡夜簿，拿指头点着一行一行往下念：「十月初一至初九，药园丢灵草十株。初八起，沈小满巡夜；初十以后，一株没丢，外加灵兽一只，狰，入册。另议的那一笔，今天议——」他从抽屉里一块一块地往外数，「——一、二、三……十块。」

小满看着那十块灵石，没有伸手。周衡道：「腊八结账，结在晚上。」他把账簿合上，难得多说了一句：「《礼记》上说，古时候天子年底祭『蜡』，连吃田鼠的猫都请来谢。用过人家的，一定要还。连猫的账，都结。」小满把灵石揣进怀里，走到门口，回过头来叫了一声：「……周师兄。」周衡道：「嗯，还有事？」小满说：「有前途。」周衡咳嗽一声，耳朵根「腾」地红了，算盘珠子拨错了两颗，挥挥手，叫他滚了。

钱掌柜在老槐树底下收摊，算盘还没收进袖子，看见阿禾过来，抬起眼皮。阿禾把那张折成一小块的纸条打开，摊在秤盘上，面无表情：「掌柜的，我押的那一文，输了。」钱掌柜道：「输了。」阿禾道：「纸条还你。」钱掌柜收了纸条，那一文钱，早在他布袋里了。阿禾站了一站，从怀里摸出小本子，翻开，拿炭条一笔一笔地写，写完了，合上，转身走了。

他站在老槐树底下，先是笑，笑出了声，笑得肋下那根骨头一抽一抽地疼；笑着笑着，眼睛便热了，热得看不清那棵槐树。他拿手背揩了揩眼睛，揩完了，还在笑。那一文钱，是她娘缝在她衣角里的，初七那天她拿剪子挑开了线。阿禾走出去几步，回过头来，看了他一眼，道：「你今天没藏。」小满没说话，右手攥着，没有张开。她只说了两个字：「藏好。」

那天夜里，柴房的门闩上了，柴墩上支起了伙房大娘借给他的一口豁了边的铁锅。那罐牛脂甘露，上午碎在了五行台上，一半叫卢方的鞋底带走了，台边那块青石，这时候还是香的。可十月里那一罐是拿什么换的，小满记得：一根牛骨头。伙房大娘那锅汤刚熬完，正把骨头往外倒，他讨了两根——熬得发白，一丝肉星也不剩——一根一根丢进了饭桶，送了两口灵气。周衡给的十块灵石揣在怀里，他一块也没动。「咯嘣」，「咯嘣」，「咔哒」。

铁锅一滚，花椒味冲得小狰连打了三个喷嚏。孙二狗是他拉来的，捧着一只碗，看着那口锅，半天没敢动。银月钻了出来，蹲在锅沿上，两只前爪举过头顶：「今晚火锅——耶～～」那一声，只小满听得见。她吃得极快：孙二狗夹起一片腊肉，吹了三口，低头一看，筷子上空了；锅里的豆腐，眼看着一块一块少下去。孙二狗揉了揉眼睛，看看锅，看看小满，小声道：「沈师兄，这锅……漏？」小满道：「是有点漏。」银月拿那根牙签——饭桶头一回吐的那一根——剔了剔牙，剔完了，又拿它串了三块豆腐。

吃到后来，锅里只剩两半汤。银月仰面躺在锅沿上，肚皮滚圆，拿牙签剔着牙，懒懒地道：「这锅底不坏。哪家铺子的？」小满道：「伙房大娘熬了三遍汤，扔出来的骨头。」银月的牙签停在了半空：「……本王吃的，是第四遍？」小满没理她。他看着柴垛底下那只饭桶，在肚里过了一遍：柴火棍换牙签，一根残株换九道纹的回春丹，两块灵石换一毒一解两颗丹；一根骨头换一罐，两根骨头，换两半。它不是乱吐的——喂什么，喂多少，喂的什么成色，便吐什么。这笔账，他没处写，记在了肚子里。

这一夜，满观说的都是一件事：一个四层的外门弟子，把卢方扔下了台，把秦雁打了下去，把马小宝的镜子照裂了，末了，叫祁不退退了一步——「他凭什么？」「运气。」「运气能连着撞上四回？」大通铺上，马小宝裹着被子抖了半夜，只说了一句：「镜子照着他……他手底下，亮了。」没人理他。

人都睡下了，孙二狗摸到他铺前，小声道：「卢师兄那一脚，你替我还了。」小满道：「他自己踩滑的。」「我坐在石阶上，闻见花椒味了。」隔了一会儿，黑地里又道：「沈师兄，明天替我写封信。就写：娘，我倒了七回，起来了七回。」他顿了一顿：「别写是谁把我打倒的。」
story_full.en:
The champion: one Foundation Pill. The Abbot put the jade case into Qi Changsong's hands. The jade was bluish-white, and across the lid was a seal strip stamped with the Abbot's great seal. Before the case was even opened, a thread of clean, bitter medicinal fragrance had seeped from the crack, cold, like pine needles on an early morning in the twelfth month, and the front rows breathed it in without meaning to, and when they had, their chests went cool, then warm. Qi Changsong took it in both hands, knelt, and knocked his head to the ground once; when he got up, the rims of his eyes were red. Zhou Heng opened the blue-covered register and turned back a few dozen pages, to the page with the stroke drawn through it, looked at it once, and only then turned forward again to a new page and handed the brush to the steward who called the names.

Xiaoman was poked down out of the tree by the kitchen woman with a washing pole. As she poked, she muttered: "...You child."

He landed and walked off past the stage, and the crowd parted of its own accord to make a path. Wherever he passed, nobody laughed at him; a good many looked at him, looked for a long time. The Abbot rose from the bamboo chair, came up to him, and said mildly: "Fourth layer now. After New Year, move to the inner sect." He paused, and said: "In the Sunken Cauldron secret realm there's a stone chamber. For three hundred years, nobody has been in it..." He didn't finish. He patted Xiaoman's shoulder, turned and left. Xiaoman stood there, and all the sweat on his back broke out at once.

Ma Xiaobao was carried back to the long bunk between two hangers-on, his face smeared with the kitchen woman's badger fat, both eyes bound with cloth, the cracked mirror still gripped in his hand; even when he'd fallen he hadn't let it go. Master Chu lifted his eyelid and looked: "Scorched. Keep them bound three days, and he won't go blind." He was fifth layer, and his name had been added to the inner sect's register too; that same evening an elder named Cui sent someone to take him in as a disciple. But all the way back he didn't say a word, only turned his bound face away, towards the Si. The Ma family's boat had already gone.

Xiaoman looked over towards the mountain gate. Elder Qu stood on the steps, leaning on his broom, watching too. But what Elder Qu was watching wasn't him. It was the jade case in Qi Changsong's hands. It was a long look, too long to be a look at a case; more like a look at something from many years ago. Then Elder Qu turned round and went on sweeping.

At the foot of the steps, Master Chu was waiting for him. Everyone had scattered towards the kitchen, and the old master stood there alone and held out two fingers to him: "Give me your wrist." Xiaoman held out his left wrist. Master Chu didn't take it: "Not that one. The other." Xiaoman stood a moment, then brought his right hand out of his sleeve. Master Chu felt it for a long time, so long that over by the mountain gate Elder Qu's broom started up again. He let go and said: "The pulse says fourth layer, same as the register." He stroked his goatee once, turned and left; three steps off, without looking back, he added one thing: "The Ma boy. That wasn't backlash."

When it got dark, Zhou Heng lit the half candle in the stewards' office. When Xiaoman went in, he already had the night-watch book open and was reading down it line by line with his finger: "First to ninth of the tenth month, ten spirit herbs lost from the herb garden. From the eighth, Shen Xiaoman on night watch; after the tenth, not one lost, plus one spirit beast, a Zheng, entered in the register. The item to be settled separately, settled today—" He counted them out of the drawer one at a time. "—one, two, three... ten."

Xiaoman looked at the ten spirit stones and didn't reach for them. Zhou Heng said: "Accounts close at Laba. They close in the evening." He shut the ledger and, for once, said one thing more: "The *Book of Rites* says that in ancient times, at the year's end, the Son of Heaven held the *zha* sacrifice, and even the cats that ate the field mice were invited and thanked. When you've used what's someone else's, you must pay it back. Even the cats' accounts get settled." Xiaoman put the spirit stones in his robe, went to the door, turned round and said: "...Senior Brother Zhou." Zhou Heng said: "Mm. Something else?" Xiaoman said: "You'll go far." Zhou Heng coughed, and the roots of his ears went red all at once; he pushed two abacus beads the wrong way and waved him out.

Shopkeeper Qian was packing up his stall under the old pagoda tree, the abacus not yet back in his sleeve, when he saw Ahe coming and lifted his eyelids. Ahe unfolded the little square of paper and laid it flat on the steelyard pan, her face blank: "Shopkeeper, that copper I bet. It lost." Shopkeeper Qian said: "It lost." Ahe said: "Here's your slip back." Shopkeeper Qian took the slip; the copper was long since in his cloth bag. Ahe stood a moment, took her little notebook out of her robe, opened it, and wrote in it stroke by stroke with charcoal; when she had finished she closed it, turned and left.

Xiaoman stood under the old pagoda tree and first laughed, laughed out loud, laughed till the bone in his side twinged and twinged; and laughing, his eyes went hot, so hot he couldn't see the pagoda tree clearly. He wiped his eyes with the back of his hand, and when he'd wiped them, he was still laughing. That one copper coin her mother had sewn into the hem of her clothes; on the seventh she had picked the thread open with scissors. Ahe went a few steps, looked back, gave him one look, and said: "You didn't hide today." Xiaoman said nothing. His right hand was clenched, and he didn't open it. She said only two words: "Hide well."

That night the woodshed door was bolted, and on the chopping block stood an iron pot with a chipped rim that the kitchen woman had lent him. The jar of Beef Tallow Sweet Dew had broken on the Five Phases Stage that morning, half of it carried off on the sole of Lu Fang's shoe, and the bluestone at the stage's edge still smelled good now. But what the jar in the tenth month had been traded for, Xiaoman remembered: one beef bone. The kitchen woman had just finished a pot of broth and was tipping out the bones, and he'd begged two (boiled white, not a shred of meat left) and dropped them one at a time into the Rice Bucket and fed it two breaths of spirit qi. The ten spirit stones Zhou Heng had given him were in his robe, and he hadn't touched one. *Crunch. Crunch. Click.*

When the iron pot came to the boil, the smell of Sichuan pepper made the little zheng sneeze three times running. Sun Ergou, whom Xiaoman had dragged along, held a bowl and looked at the pot and for a long while didn't dare move. Yinyue came out, crouched on the pot's rim, and raised both front paws over her head: "Hotpot tonight—yaaay~~" Only Xiaoman could hear it. She ate very fast. Sun Ergou picked up a slice of cured pork, blew on it three times, looked down, and his chopsticks were empty; the tofu in the pot went down a piece at a time before his eyes. Sun Ergou rubbed his eyes, looked at the pot, looked at Xiaoman, and said quietly: "Senior Brother Shen, this pot... does it leak?" Xiaoman said: "It leaks a bit." Yinyue picked her teeth with the toothpick (the very first thing the Rice Bucket ever spat out), and when she'd picked them she skewered three pieces of tofu on it.

By the end there were only two half-portions of broth left in the pot. Yinyue lay on her back on the pot's rim, her belly round, picking her teeth with the toothpick, and said lazily: "Not a bad broth base. Which shop's it from?" Xiaoman said: "Bones the kitchen woman threw out after boiling broth three times." Yinyue's toothpick stopped in mid-air: "...What this queen ate was the fourth boiling?" Xiaoman ignored her. He looked at the Rice Bucket under the woodpile and went over it in his head: a firewood stick for a toothpick, one leftover stalk for a Spring-Return Pill of nine lines, two spirit stones for two pills, a poison and its cure; one bone for one jar, two bones for two halves. It didn't spit things out at random: what you fed it, how much, of what quality, that was what came out. This account he had nowhere to write. He kept it in his head.

That night the whole abbey talked about one thing: an outer-sect disciple of the fourth layer had thrown Lu Fang off the stage, knocked Qin Yan off, cracked Ma Xiaobao's mirror, and at the end made Qi Who Doesn't Step Back take a step back. "How did he do it?" "Luck." "Luck four times running?" In the long bunk, Ma Xiaobao lay wrapped in his quilt shaking half the night, and said only one thing: "The mirror shone on him... and under his hand, something lit up." Nobody paid him any attention.

When everyone was asleep, Sun Ergou felt his way to Xiaoman's bunk and said quietly: "That stamp of Senior Brother Lu's. You paid it back for me." Xiaoman said: "He slipped by himself." "I was sitting on the steps. I smelled the Sichuan pepper." After a while the dark spoke again: "Senior Brother Shen, write a letter for me tomorrow. Just write: Ma, I fell down seven times and got up seven times." He paused. "Don't write who knocked me down."

exits.means: rests, ends the day, or asks what comes next

story.zh:
小满在铺上一笔一笔地写：**娘：我进仙门了。一年五两，观里说腊月就送到家。屋顶修一修。盆可以收起来了，十七个都收。我在这里很好。有人欺负我，我记着账。有几笔，已经还上了。——小满**

小满把信折好，又打开来，在最底下添了一行：**娘，漏勺也能打水。**他握着胸口的木牌，小声道：「你欠我的那张饼……还欠着吧？」木牌轻轻地，烫了一下。

隔了一会儿，银月的声音很低，一点也不懒：「镜子裂的那一下，镜子那头，有人。」小满一下子坐了起来：「哪头？」银月道：「很远。西边。本王只听见一句。」「叫徐州那个，十月去邺城等着。」

小满在黑地里坐了很久，才道：「那面镜子，找的是你。」「是本王。」银月道。「他主子要本王的命。」她顿了一顿，「本王在谁身上，他找谁。」

「本王欠你一张饼。」银月又道，声音低下去，「这一笔，怕是还不上了。」小满把木牌攥紧了，攥得指节发白：「欠着。利息另算。」徐州那个，十月去邺城等着——邺城在哪里，他不知道。他心想：这一句，记住了。
story.en:
Xiaoman wrote on the bunk, stroke by stroke: **Ma: I've got into the immortals' sect. Five taels a year; the abbey says it'll reach home in the twelfth month. Fix the roof. You can put the basins away now, all seventeen. I'm very well here. When people bully me, I keep an account. A few of the items are paid back already. —Xiaoman**

Xiaoman folded the letter, opened it again, and added one line at the very bottom: **Ma, a leaky ladle can carry water too.** He held the wooden tablet on his chest and said quietly: "That flatbread you owe me... still owe it, right?" The tablet went warm, gently, once.

After a while Yinyue's voice came, very low, not lazy at all: "When the mirror cracked, there was someone at the other end of it." Xiaoman sat bolt upright: "Which end?" Yinyue said: "Far away. West. This queen only heard one sentence." "Tell the one in Xu to go to Ye in the tenth month and wait."

Xiaoman sat in the dark a long time before he said: "That mirror. What it was looking for was you." "It was this queen," said Yinyue. "His master wants this queen's life." She paused. "Whoever this queen is on, he looks for them."

"This queen owes you a flatbread," Yinyue said again, her voice dropping. "That debt, I'm afraid, can't be paid now." Xiaoman gripped the tablet tight, till his knuckles went white: "Owe it. Interest extra." Tell the one in Xu to go to Ye in the tenth month and wait. Where Ye was, he didn't know. He thought: that sentence, I've got it.

story_full.zh:
孙二狗走了以后，小满趴在铺上，就着窗外的月光，给家里写第一封信。他头一句写的是「娘，我当上仙人了」，擦了；第二句写「娘，我打赢了马小宝」，想了想，这话要是传到村里，马三怕是要上门，又擦了。

小满在铺上一笔一笔地写：**娘：我进仙门了。一年五两，观里说腊月就送到家。屋顶修一修。盆可以收起来了，十七个都收。给我爹买一副护膝，狗皮的。给吴婆婆，再送一条鹿腿，这回是买的。我在这里很好。有人欺负我，我记着账。有几笔，已经还上了。——小满**

小满把信折好，想了想，又打开来，在最底下添了一行：**娘，漏勺也能打水。**信压在枕头底下，明天一早交给周衡，跟沈家那一包五两银子一车送下山。弓就搁在枕头边上，他伸手摸了摸那十七道牛筋。他握着胸口的木牌，小声道：「你欠我的那张饼……还欠着吧？」木牌轻轻地，烫了一下。像是在说：**还欠着。**

隔了一会儿，银月的声音很低，一点也不懒：「镜子裂的那一下，镜子那头，有人。」小满一下子坐了起来：「哪头？」银月道：「很远。西边。本王只听见一句。」她顿了一顿，学那个声音，学得很平，平得没有一点起伏：「叫徐州那个，十月去邺城等着。」

小满在黑地里坐了很久，才道：「那面镜子，找的是你。」

「是本王。」银月道。她头一回没有摆本王的架子，声音平平的，「正月初五，柴垛底下端镜子的那个人，说本王是死的。他回去，便是这么报的。今天，那面镜子到了台上，照了一照——本王没死，在你身上。」

「他要你做什么？」

「他主子要本王的命。」她顿了一顿，「本王在谁身上，他找谁。」

「今天台下几千双眼睛，都看见了，沉鼎观，外门，四层，沈小满。」她又道，「镜子那头的人，也看见了。」

小满在黑地里，半天没说话。

「本王欠你一张饼。」银月又道，声音低下去，「这一笔，怕是还不上了。」

小满把木牌攥紧了，攥得指节发白：「欠着。利息另算。」

木牌没有烫，也没有凉，就那么贴着他的手心，温温的，像一只蜷着的小东西。徐州那个，十月去邺城等着——邺城在哪里，他不知道。他心想：这一句，记住了。
story_full.en:
When Sun Ergou had gone, Xiaoman lay on his front on the bunk and, by the moonlight from the window, wrote his first letter home. The first line he wrote was "Ma, I've become an immortal," and he rubbed it out. The second was "Ma, I beat Ma Xiaobao"; he thought about it, and if that got back to the village Ma San might come to the door, so he rubbed it out too.

Xiaoman wrote on the bunk, stroke by stroke: **Ma: I've got into the immortals' sect. Five taels a year; the abbey says it'll reach home in the twelfth month. Fix the roof. You can put the basins away now, all seventeen. Buy Pa a pair of knee pads, dog-skin ones. Take Granny Wu another leg of venison, and this time a bought one. I'm very well here. When people bully me, I keep an account. A few of the items are paid back already. —Xiaoman**

Xiaoman folded the letter, thought about it, opened it again, and added one line at the very bottom: **Ma, a leaky ladle can carry water too.** He put the letter under his pillow, to give to Zhou Heng first thing in the morning, to go down the mountain in the same cart as the Shen family's packet of five taels. The bow lay by his pillow; he reached out and felt its seventeen layers of ox sinew. He held the wooden tablet on his chest and said quietly: "That flatbread you owe me... still owe it, right?" The tablet went warm, gently, once. As if to say: **Still owe it.**

After a while Yinyue's voice came, very low, not lazy at all: "When the mirror cracked, there was someone at the other end of it." Xiaoman sat bolt upright: "Which end?" Yinyue said: "Far away. West. This queen only heard one sentence." She paused, and mimicked the voice, very flat, flat without a single rise or fall: "Tell the one in Xu to go to Ye in the tenth month and wait."

Xiaoman sat in the dark a long time before he said: "That mirror. What it was looking for was you."

"It was this queen," said Yinyue. For the first time she didn't put on this queen's airs; her voice was flat. "On the fifth of the first month, the one holding the mirror under the woodpile said this queen was dead. That's what he went back and reported. Today the mirror came onto the stage and shone once, and this queen isn't dead. She's on you."

"What does he want you for?"

"His master wants this queen's life." She paused. "Whoever this queen is on, he looks for them."

"Thousands of eyes below the stage today all saw it: Sunken Cauldron Abbey, outer sect, fourth layer, Shen Xiaoman," she went on. "The person at the other end of the mirror saw it too."

Xiaoman said nothing in the dark for a long time.

"This queen owes you a flatbread," Yinyue said again, her voice dropping. "That debt, I'm afraid, can't be paid now."

Xiaoman gripped the tablet tight, till his knuckles went white: "Owe it. Interest extra."

The tablet didn't go hot, and didn't go cold. It just lay against his palm, warm, like a small curled-up thing. Tell the one in Xu to go to Ye in the tenth month and wait. Where Ye was, he didn't know. He thought: that sentence, I've got it.
